userStories.title: Review findings carry a trigger class
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry a trigger class and evidence from the PR review reply through to agreed findings and inline comments.

**Motivation** — #2988: findings have a severity but no trigger, so a finding that needs a forged mtime blocks exactly like one reachable in normal use.

**Approach** — **Shared vocabulary.** New `packages/nax/src/workflow/blocking-findings/index.ts`, a nested barrel imported as `@/workflow/blocking-findings` (not through the `@/workflow` barrel, which imports `@/operations` and `@/config` and would close an import cycle from `config/schemas-bot.ts` and `operations/bot-pr-review-reply.ts`; `bun run check:import-cycles` must stay at its baseline). It uses only `import type` for `PrComment`, `WorkflowSeverity` and config types. `bot/` already imports `workflow/`; `workflow/` never imports `bot/`.

`PrFinding` (`operations/bot-types.ts`) gains optional `trigger?: FindingTrigger` and `triggerEvidence?: string`. `parsePrReviewReply` (`operations/bot-pr-review-reply.ts`) always sets `trigger` with `parseFindingTrigger(entry.trigger)` and keeps `triggerEvidence` when it is a non-empty string, trimmed and capped at 300 characters. `TASK_CONTRACT` (`prompts/builders/bot-pr-review-builder.ts`) adds `"trigger": "normal|own-concurrency|adversarial|manual", "triggerEvidence": "..."` to the finding shape and one definition line per class, worded as what to report:
- `normal`: reachable in ordinary use of the product
- `own-concurrency`: needs two of the tool's own processes or sessions interleaving
- `adversarial`: needs a deliberate actor (forged metadata, input the threat model excludes, shadowed builtins)
- `manual`: needs a human acting on the checkout or state mid-operation
The finding arm of `AgreedItem` (`bot/post.ts`) gains optional `trigger?: FindingTrigger` and `triggerEvidence?: string`; `agreedItems` copies each when present on the verdict finding. Final combined design (US-002 supplies the shared reader): `mergeEarlier` sets `trigger` from `readFindingThreadFacts` of the earlier thread's first comment only when that comment has a `Trigger:` line, and removes `Trigger:` lines from the earlier item's `issue`. `renderFindingComment` (`bot/render-comments.ts`) takes `PrFinding`-shaped input and adds, after the issue and a blank line, and before the suggestion paragraph, the line `Trigger: <class>` followed by ` - <evidence>` when evidence is present, only when `trigger` is set; evidence goes through `safeText`. The finding's key (`findingKey`) is unchanged.

For this first story, implement the earlier-thread trigger read using the trigger-only primitives; US-002 supplies the shared thread reader. Update the exact expected contract literal in `test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder.test.ts:47` and the expected parsed draft in `test/unit/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.test.ts:79` (add `trigger: "normal"`), leaving other existing assertions unchanged.

**Scope** — In: PR reply, agreed finding metadata, earlier findings and inline rendering. Out: US-002 config/predicate, US-003 blocking policy decisions, US-005 lineage, and workflow branch review findings.

**Interface**
```typescript
export const FINDING_TRIGGERS = ["normal", "own-concurrency", "adversarial", "manual"] as const;
export type FindingTrigger = (typeof FINDING_TRIGGERS)[number];
/** Missing or unknown reads as "normal", so an unclassified finding still blocks. */
export function parseFindingTrigger(value: unknown): FindingTrigger;
```
`PrFinding` adds `readonly trigger?: FindingTrigger; readonly triggerEvidence?: string`. `AgreedItem` adds `trigger?: FindingTrigger; triggerEvidence?: string` to the finding arm.

[unit] parseFindingTrigger returns "normal" for undefined, for "race" and for the number 3.

[unit] parsePrReviewReply on a reply whose finding has "trigger": "adversarial" and "triggerEvidence": "  forged mtime on the claim file  " returns a finding with trigger: "adversarial" and triggerEvidence: "forged mtime on the claim file".

userStories.title: Apply the blocking set to review posting and readiness
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Use the same effective PR policy to decide which new findings get inline threads and which agreed findings hold readiness.

**Motivation** — A scope ruling posted as a PR comment worked only as long as the reviewer re-read it.

**Approach** — `nax bot review` (`bot/review-run.ts`, while building the review env, through a new helper module `bot/review-convergence.ts` so `review-run.ts` (496 lines) grows by no more than the call) computes `effectiveBlockingTriggers` from the PR's top-level comments, the writer set it already reads (`readWriters`, `bot/writers.ts:20`) and `configuredBlockingTriggers(config)`, and passes it on `PostReviewInput` as `blockingTriggers`, `blockingSource` and `ignoredScopeRulings`. Then:
- `postFindings` (`bot/post.ts`) handles a critical or important finding that has a file and line and is not blocking under that set the way it handles a minor today: no new inline thread, an existing own thread for the key is still edited (and that finding is then not listed as residual), and it is returned in a new `residual` list. A non-blocking finding with no file or line stays in `offLine`, as today.
- `ReviewSummaryInput` (`bot/render-comments.ts`) gains `residual?`, `blockingTriggers?`, `blockingSource?` and `ignoredScopeRulings?`. The summary renders `### Residual findings (not blocking)` with `- <Severity> <file>:<line>: <issue> (trigger <class> - <evidence>)` per residual, all author text through `safeText`; a line `Blocking triggers: <a>, <b> (config)` or `Blocking triggers: <a> (PR comment by @<author>)`; and `Ignored scope ruling: <first line>` per ignored comment.
- `BotReviewArtifact` (`bot/post.ts`) gains optional `blockingTriggers?: readonly FindingTrigger[]`, the effective set.
- New `reviewBlockingTriggers(env: BotFixEnv): readonly FindingTrigger[]` (new `bot/review-blocking.ts`) returns `env.review.blockingTriggers ?? env.codeReview?.blockingTriggers ?? configuredBlockingTriggers(env.config)`, so a newer conversation-only review's set wins over the older code review's. `blockingKeys` (`bot/fix-report.ts:343`) becomes `blockingKeys(review: BotReviewArtifact, blocking: readonly FindingTrigger[]): string[]` and keeps a finding when `isBlockingFinding(item, blocking)`; `openFindingHold` passes `reviewBlockingTriggers(env)`.

Use the existing code review selection/settlement for the findings themselves, not for policy precedence. Legacy post fixtures without triggers read normal and old artifacts fall back to config. Preserve the source line budget in `fix-report.ts`.

**Scope** — In: review environment, residuals, policy notice and artifact, readiness predicate. Out: US-005 lineage/history prompt, US-007 fix short-circuit, US-008 status and blocker counts; no new inline threads for minor or residual findings.

**Interface** — `PostReviewInput` adds `blockingTriggers?`, `blockingSource?`, `ignoredScopeRulings?`; `ReviewSummaryInput` adds `residual?`, `blockingTriggers?`, `blockingSource?`, `ignoredScopeRulings?`; `BotReviewArtifact` adds `blockingTriggers?: readonly FindingTrigger[]`.
```typescript
function reviewBlockingTriggers(env: BotFixEnv): readonly FindingTrigger[];
function blockingKeys(review: BotReviewArtifact, blocking: readonly FindingTrigger[]): string[];
```

routing.reasoning: Wires permission-checked scope into review, artifacts and readiness; authorization regressions can release a hold incorrectly.

userStories.title: Attribute bot review findings to earlier fix pushes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Compute lineage from the blamed anchor commit and show earlier bot pushes inside the incremental review range.

**Motivation** — #2982 and #2987 (points 1 and 3): no record links a finding to the bot fix that wrote its lines, so no signal says the findings are chasing their own fixes.

**Approach** — New `packages/nax/src/bot/lineage.ts` with `computeLineage(input: { targets: readonly { readonly key: string; readonly file?: string; readonly line?: number }[]; entries: readonly BotPushEntry[]; worktree: string; head: string }, deps = _lineageDeps): Promise<{ lineage: ReadonlyMap<string, FindingLineage>; unknown: ReadonlySet<string>; unreachable: number }>` keyed by target `key`. Exit codes: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0 is yes and exit 1 is no; any other exit code or a spawn failure is an error. Procedure: an entry is reachable when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <entry.sha> <head>` exits 0; an entry whose check exits 1, or errors, is skipped and counted in `unreachable` (an error is also logged at warn). For each target with `file` and `line`, `git blame --porcelain -L <line>,<line> <head> -- <file>` names commit `C`; the newest reachable entry for which `C` equals `entry.sha`, or `C` is an ancestor of `entry.sha` and not of `entry.base`, is the match. A match gives `{ generation: 1 + max(entry.items' generation, 0), parents: entry.items' keys, pushSha: entry.sha }`; no match gives no lineage (generation 0). A `git blame` exiting non-zero, or a matching ancestry check that errors (not exit 1), puts the target's key in `unknown`. `_lineageDeps.runGit` is injectable. Wiring: while building the review env (`reviewEnvironment`), `bot/review-convergence.ts` reads the ledger from the bot's own `fix-summary` comment and, for an incremental range, selects the prompt's `botPushes` with `_botReviewDeps.isAncestor`; `PostReviewInput` gains `botPushes?: readonly BotPushEntry[]` and `worktree?`, read only by the review graph's `post` node. That node (`bot/review-run.ts`) runs `computeLineage` with `{ runGit: _botReviewDeps.runGit }` before calling `postPrReview` and passes the result as `PostReviewInput.lineage?: { lineage; unknown; unreachable }`. Its targets are every verdict finding (keyed by `findingKey`) and every open earlier thread that has `path` and `line` (keyed by the same key `mergeEarlier` gives its item), so a finding carried over from an earlier round keeps its lineage. `agreedItems` copies `lineage` / `lineageUnknown` onto the finding items; `BotReviewArtifact` gains optional `unreachablePushes?: number`. `renderFindingComment` adds, on the line directly after the trigger line (or after the issue and a blank line when there is no trigger), `Lineage: generation <n>, on lines added by nax bot fix <sha7> for <parent keys joined ", ">` when lineage is present. For an incremental review, `PrReviewInput` (`bot/review-step.ts`) and `BotPrReviewPromptInput` gain `botPushes?: readonly BotPushEntry[]`, the reachable entries whose `sha` is not an ancestor of the range base; `reviewPrompt` passes them and the prompt renders a section `## Earlier nax bot fix pushes in this range` with one line per item: `- <base7>..<sha7>: nax bot fix for <key> (<issue>), generation <n>`. No sentence in that section says what to do with it. `mergeEarlier` also removes `Lineage:` lines from an earlier item's `issue`.

The post-side `botPushes` is the full available ledger for reachability/lineage, not the prompt's range-filtered subset; recover the owned top-level summary from the forge data already loaded for review. No own summary or empty ledger means no blame. Treat an unreadable ledger as empty and warn. `_botReviewDeps.isAncestor` throws on a Git error (`bot/review-deps.ts:35-47`); omit an entry whose range membership cannot be proved without aborting the review or losing the full ledger needed by the post node. When a finding's Git check is unknown, set `lineageUnknown: true` without a lineage line and continue. Use `effectiveEarlier` (`bot/post-earlier.ts:41`) to match `mergeEarlier`'s keys, with lineage limited to open `f-` findings. US-003 authors `review-convergence.ts`; keep history logic independently usable from `lineage.ts` with only the binding dependencies, and compose the helper calls in the combined tree. Use type-only prompt imports for ledger interfaces.

**Scope** — In: bot finding ancestry, earlier bot finding attribution, artifact and inline metadata, and incremental prompt facts. Out: US-003 blocking policy, US-006 fixer facts, US-008 chain notice, lineage for `w-` findings, advisor routing, and changing `reviewRange` or forcing full reviews.

**Interface**
```typescript
function computeLineage(input: { targets: readonly { readonly key: string; readonly file?: string; readonly line?: number }[]; entries: readonly BotPushEntry[]; worktree: string; head: string }, deps = _lineageDeps): Promise<{ lineage: ReadonlyMap<string, FindingLineage>; unknown: ReadonlySet<string>; unreachable: number }>;
renderFindingComment(finding: WorkflowFindingDraft & { trigger?: FindingTrigger; triggerEvidence?: string; lineage?: FindingLineage }): string;
```
`PostReviewInput` adds `botPushes?: readonly BotPushEntry[]`, `worktree?` and `lineage?: { lineage; unknown; unreachable }`; `BotReviewArtifact` adds `unreachablePushes?: number`; `PrReviewInput` and `BotPrReviewPromptInput` add `botPushes?: readonly BotPushEntry[]`.

[integration] runBotReview on an incremental range with a reachable ledger entry after the range base passes the review op a prompt containing that entry's line under ## Earlier nax bot fix pushes in this range.
[integration] runBotReview on a PR with no own fix-summary comment writes agreed findings with no lineage key and runs no git blame.
[integration] postPrReview with an open earlier thread whose first comment has a Lineage: line writes a merged earlier finding item whose issue has no Lineage: line.

[unit] computeLineage whose stubbed reachability check exits 128 for an entry skips that entry, counts it in unreachable and puts no target in unknown for it.

[unit] When a target's matching merge-base --is-ancestor check errors (non-0/1 exit code or spawn failure), computeLineage records the key in unknown with no lineage; exit 1 alone is a normal negative answer.
[integration] When a finding's blame fails or a matching ancestry check errors, runBotReview continues and writes the finding with lineageUnknown: true and no lineage.

routing.reasoning: New Git attribution algorithm with explicit exit semantics, two review data paths, and forge/artifact outputs.

userStories.title: Give the fixer trigger, lineage and growth facts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Surface finding facts and prior out-of-declaration additions in the fix prompt without telling the fixer how to act on them.

**Motivation** — Each finding was real, but each round's findings sat increasingly on the previous round's fix (a tie check grew a lock, the lock grew claim files, the claim files grew a reclaim path, each drawing an Important finding).

**Approach** — `BotPrFixPromptInput` (`prompts/builders/bot-pr-fix-builder.ts`) gains `findingFacts?: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly lines: readonly string[] }[]` and `outsideGrowth?: readonly { readonly path: string; readonly added: number }[]`. `buildBotPrFixPrompt` renders, when either is non-empty, a section `## Facts about these findings`: per finding `- <id>:` then its lines indented; then, when `outsideGrowth` is non-empty, ``Lines added by earlier nax bot fix pushes on this PR in files outside the feature's declared files: `<path>` +<n>, ...`` (largest first, at most 10, then `and <k> more`). Per-finding lines (new `bot/fix-facts.ts`, `findingFactLines(item, ledger, blocking)`): `Trigger: <class>` plus ` - <evidence>` when the item has a trigger; `Lineage: generation <n>, on lines added by nax bot fix <sha7> for <key> (<issue>)` per parent, the issue taken from the ledger item; `Not blocking readiness (minor or trigger outside the blocking set)` when `isBlockingFinding` is false; nothing for thread and comment items. `outsideDeclaredGrowth(input, deps)` in `bot/fix-facts.ts`: the feature's declared files are the union over the PRD's stories (PRD from `featureIntentPaths(env.checkout).prdPath`, loaded with `loadPRD`) of `contextFiles` paths, `expectedFiles` and `modifiedFiles` paths, each also joined with the story's `workdir` when it has one; for each ledger entry, `git diff --numstat <base> <sha>` (through injectable `deps.runGit`, in the checkout worktree) gives added lines per path; paths outside the declared set are summed. No PRD, an unreadable PRD or a failed diff gives `undefined` (logged at debug). `fixStep` (`bot/fix-steps.ts`) passes both to `buildBotPrFixPrompt`; `toFixFindings` and `WorkflowFinding` are unchanged.

Use the own fix-summary ledger and effective blocking policy: latest artifact, code-review artifact, then configured defaults. Preserve optional rendering and existing fix/repair prompt behavior when inputs are absent. Agents receive facts, never orders: no prompt text tells them what to do with a trigger or a lineage.

**Scope** — In: prompt facts, PRD declared-path union and numstat aggregation. Out: US-004 ledger persistence, US-005 reviewer attribution, US-007 whether the fix session runs, and asking before acting on a minor that asks to revert an earlier bot change.

**Interface** — `findingFactLines(item, ledger, blocking)` and `outsideDeclaredGrowth(input, deps)` in `bot/fix-facts.ts`. `BotPrFixPromptInput` adds:
```typescript
findingFacts?: readonly { readonly id: string; readonly lines: readonly string[] }[];
outsideGrowth?: readonly { readonly path: string; readonly added: number }[];
```

userStories.title: Skip the fix session for non-blocking-only findings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Avoid a fix session and fix push when agreed work consists only of non-blocking findings, and show the follow-ups.

**Motivation** — #2979: `nax bot fix` acts on every agreed item, minor ones included, while readiness waits only on critical and important ones; a minor posted only in the summary triggered a push that reversed a human's decision and reset readiness.

**Approach** — `BotFixState` (`bot/fix-steps.ts`) gains `followUps?: readonly { readonly key: string; readonly severity: WorkflowSeverity; readonly trigger: FindingTrigger }[]`, and the `fix` node's `produces` in `bot/fix-run.ts` gains `"followUps"` (the step graph rejects an undeclared patch key, `step-graph/run.ts:76`). `fixStep` returns `{ patch: { agreedCount, outcome: "nothing", followUps }, exit: "nothing" }` without starting a fix session when `env.review.agreed` is non-empty and no item is push-worthy; an item is push-worthy when it is a `thread` or `comment` item, or a `finding` for which `isBlockingFinding(item, reviewBlockingTriggers(env))` holds. `followUps` lists each agreed finding's key, severity and trigger (`normal` when absent). The fix summary's `nothing` text (in `bot/fix-outcome-text.ts`) reads `No fix session: no agreed item can hold readiness. Left for follow-up: <key> (<Severity>, <trigger>), ...` (at most 10, then `and <k> more`) when `followUps` is non-empty, and `Nothing to fix: the latest review agreed with no item.` otherwise. When something is push-worthy, every agreed item still goes to the fixer as today. If the later ledger node pushes the advisor ledger, the existing `Pushed <sha>: advisor ledger.` line is listed first and the follow-up line after it.

`initialFixState` can start directly at `check` after `reuseSavedFix` (`bot/fix-run.ts:283-287`; `bot/saved-fix.ts:123-149`), bypassing `fixStep`. Apply the same push-worthiness decision before reusing saved work for a non-empty agreed list. Route a non-blocking-only list to the existing `fix` start so `fixStep` emits `followUps`; preserve existing reuse for push-worthy reviews, ready-only, setup checks, and advisor-ledger carry.

In existing session-driving fixtures change only the agreed finding severity from minor to important so the same fix path remains exercised. In `test/integration/bot/` these are `checkout.test.ts`, `fix-check-steps.test.ts`, `fix-ready-only.test.ts`, `cost-guard.test.ts`, `fix-pinned-session.test.ts`, `fix-session.test.ts`, `fix-run.test.ts` (fixture at line 160), `fix-trust.test.ts`, `in-place-fix.test.ts` (fixture at line 74), and `saved-fix-reuse.test.ts` (agreed list at line 43 only where the case expects reuse or a session). Preserve empty-review behavior and the ordinary advisor-ledger transition. Keep `fix-report.ts` at or under 600 lines.

**Scope** — In: gating session entry, declared graph output and follow-up summary. Out: US-006 prompt facts, US-008 push count and chain notice, a cap or hard stop on rounds, and asking before acting on a minor. The preexisting advisor-ledger-only push is not removed.

**Interface**
```typescript
followUps?: readonly { readonly key: string; readonly severity: WorkflowSeverity; readonly trigger: FindingTrigger }[];
```
`fix` node `produces` gains `"followUps"`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] fixStep with agreed items [minor finding "f-1" trigger "normal"] returns { patch: { agreedCount: 1, outcome: "nothing", followUps: [{ key: "f-1", severity: "minor", trigger: "normal" }] }, exit: "nothing" }.
[unit] fixStep with agreed items [minor finding "f-1" trigger "normal"] does not call runBranchFix.
[unit] fixStep with agreed items [important finding trigger "adversarial"] under the review's blockingTriggers ["normal", "own-concurrency"] returns outcome: "nothing".
[unit] fixStep with agreed items [important finding trigger "adversarial"] under the review's blockingTriggers ["normal", "own-concurrency"] does not call runBranchFix.

[unit] fixStep with agreed items [minor finding, agreed thread item] calls runBranchFix.
[unit] fixStep with agreed items [minor finding, agreed comment item] calls runBranchFix.
[unit] fixStep with a review artifact lacking blockingTriggers and agreed items [important finding trigger "manual"] uses the configured default set and returns outcome: "nothing".
[unit] fixStep with no agreed items returns outcome: "nothing" with no followUps key, as today.
[integration] runBotFix on a review whose only agreed item is a minor finding completes without a step-graph STEP_GRAPH_UNDECLARED_OUTPUT refusal and reports outcome nothing.

[unit] The fix summary for outcome: "nothing" with followUps [{ key: "f-1", severity: "minor", trigger: "normal" }] contains No fix session: no agreed item can hold readiness. Left for follow-up: f-1 (Minor, normal).
[unit] renderFixSummary with outcome: "nothing" and 12 followUps lists 10 follow-ups followed by the literal 'and 2 more'.
[unit] The fix summary for outcome: "nothing" with no followUps contains Nothing to fix: the latest review agreed with no item.

userStories.title: Show blocking findings and fix chains in status and summaries
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Show unsettled blockers in live workflow status and report blocker counts, fix pushes and qualifying fix-induced chains.

**Motivation** — #2981: `nax workflow status` printed `No open items.` for PR #2978 while three Important bot inline findings held readiness, because it counts only the item index.

**Approach** — New `packages/nax/src/bot/blocking-threads.ts` exports `readBlockingFindingThreads(input: { ref; threads; comments; login; configured: readonly FindingTrigger[]; deps; cwd }): Promise<readonly OpenItem[]>`: every review thread whose first comment is by `login`, carries a `nax-bot:v1` marker key starting `f-`, is not resolved, is not settled by `readSettledKeys` (`bot/rulings.ts:454`, the same reader readiness uses; its input type `SettlementReadInput` (`bot/rulings.ts:395`) becomes `Omit<RecordRulingsInput, "readModel" | "callerRulings" | "info">`, since the reader never uses `info` and the status path has only the PR URL), and for which `isBlockingFinding(readFindingThreadFacts(body), effectiveBlockingTriggers({ comments, writers, configured }).triggers)` holds, as `{ id: <key>, kind: "finding", severity, file: thread.path, line: thread.line, issue: "bot review: " + firstIssueLine(<body without marker>) }`; `writers` from `readWriters` with the forge permission check. `WorkflowForgeDeps` (`cli/workflow-forge.ts`) gains `readBlockingTriggers: (dir: string) => Promise<readonly FindingTrigger[]>`, defaulting to `configuredBlockingTriggers(await loadConfig(dir))` and to `DEFAULT_BLOCKING_TRIGGERS` when loading fails. `buildReport` (`cli/workflow.ts`), on the live path only (after `readLiveStatus` returns the live arm), reads the PR threads and comments, calls `readBlockingFindingThreads` and appends its items to `openItems`, so `No open items.` is not printed and the exit code is 2 while one exists; a failure of that read is logged at warn and adds nothing. The review summary's open-items line (`itemStatusLines`, `bot/render-comments.ts`, which gains a `blockingCount` argument from `ReviewSummaryInput.blockingCount?`) becomes `Open items: <open> of <total> indexed; <k> blocking review findings.` when `k` (agreed findings that pass `isBlockingFinding` under the effective set) is above 0, and is unchanged otherwise. New `bot/convergence-summary.ts` exports `convergenceLines(input: { entries: readonly BotPushEntry[]; unreachable: number; agreed: readonly AgreedItem[]; blocking: readonly FindingTrigger[]; noticeGeneration: number }): string[]`, called from `reportStep` with the ledger after the append, `env.review.unreachablePushes ?? 0`, `env.review.agreed`, the effective set and `configuredChainNoticeGeneration(env.config)`. It returns `nax bot fix pushes on this PR: <n>` once the ledger has an entry, with ` (<u> no longer in history)` when `u > 0`, and, when any blocking agreed finding has `lineage.generation >= noticeGeneration`, the heading `### Findings are chasing their own fixes` with one line per such finding: `- <key> (<Severity>, <trigger>), generation <n>: on lines added by nax bot fix <sha7> for <parent key> (<parent issue>)`. The section names the chain only; it carries no advice.

`cli/workflow.ts` imports `readBlockingFindingThreads` through the `@/bot` barrel (`bot/index.ts` exports it); `check:import-cycles` stays at its baseline. Strip the generated `**nax bot**` wrapper and identity marker before reading the severity prefix and issue; check opener identity independently of marker parsing. Read `ref` and `login` from the same forge identity used for the live PR; keep the enrichment failure separate from `readLiveStatus` fallback. The existing plain `itemLine` (`cli/workflow.ts:243`) omits location and severity: include the severity, path and line for the appended bot findings without changing existing indexed-item lines, and preserve the fields in JSON. Keep `fix-report.ts` at or under 600 lines. Keep current workflow-status live fixtures without a qualifying own thread byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Scope** — In: live-status enrichment, review blocking count and fix convergence facts. Out: US-005 generation computation, US-007 push decision, advisor/calling-chat routing, caps/hard stops, forge permalinks, and adding blockers when the item index is absent or the live read fails.

**Interface**
```typescript
function readBlockingFindingThreads(input: { ref; threads; comments; login; configured: readonly FindingTrigger[]; deps; cwd }): Promise<readonly OpenItem[]>;
function convergenceLines(input: { entries: readonly BotPushEntry[]; unreachable: number; agreed: readonly AgreedItem[]; blocking: readonly FindingTrigger[]; noticeGeneration: number }): string[];
type SettlementReadInput = Omit<RecordRulingsInput, "readModel" | "callerRulings" | "info">;
```
`WorkflowForgeDeps` adds `readBlockingTriggers: (dir: string) => Promise<readonly FindingTrigger[]>`; `ReviewSummaryInput` adds `blockingCount?`.

routing.reasoning: Adds a live, identity- and writer-checked read and wires two summaries; strict isolation covers permission-sensitive filters.

suggestedCriteria: When the blocking-thread read throws after a successful live draft read, nax workflow status -f <feature> --json reports no appended bot finding in openItems.

analysis:
Goal (#2988, #2979, #2981, #2982): distinguish triggers from severity, use one blocking predicate, record bot fix pushes and attribute affected lines, and expose real blockers and fix-induced chains without prescribing agent behavior. PR #2978 (11 bot review rounds, 21 Important findings) exposed the missing feedback loop. This is an enhancement of the Bun/TypeScript/Zod CLI in packages/nax; no workspace dependency or release changes. Codebase-memory tools were unavailable; source references below come from repository grep and targeted reads.

Review path (US-001/003/005): packages/nax/src/operations/bot-pr-review.ts:66 and :116 share parsePrReviewReply; packages/nax/src/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.ts:13 validates each entry via toFindingDraft and strips acId. Keep classification inside the PR adapter; generic WorkflowFindingDraft and the workflow's own branch review remain unchanged. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/bot-pr-review-builder.ts:183, :224 and :247 own the incremental and reply-contract text. packages/nax/src/bot/review-triage.ts:21-55 already reads raw top-level comments, threads, login, author IDs, a cached permission check, and a writer set over eligible triage authors. Use raw top-level comments plus the already permission-checked writers (never infer write access from a comment or model verdict). packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts:244-365 selects one range and builds both reviewer and poster inputs; :125-140 is the post node. packages/nax/src/bot/review-step.ts:101 assembles the reviewer prompt. packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts:150, :188, :270 and :397 assemble agreed items, merge earlier items, decide placement, and save before mutating the forge. packages/nax/src/bot/post-earlier.ts:41-69 centralizes earlier-thread marker/ownership, open-verdict and issue selection; it also sees w- indexed items, which are not lineage targets. Reuse the same effective earlier key for blame and merge; don't hash the rendered issue or count withdrawn/fixed earlier findings. packages/nax/src/bot/render.ts:14-27 neutralizes rendered text and keys findings only on file and normalized issue. packages/nax/src/bot/render-comments.ts:59 and :146 own the inline finding and indexed-item line. The forge wrapper prepends a bot header; read thread facts and issue text from the finding content without confusing the header or ownership marker for the severity or issue. Preserve existing own-thread edit and off-line fallback.

Policy (US-002/003/007/008): packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:467 prefaults the bot schema, but packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types.ts:383 permits absent bot; packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:66 is the help registry. Use the narrow @/workflow/blocking-findings barrel with type-only edges out; the broad workflow graph reaches operations/config, e.g. packages/nax/src/workflow/step-context.ts:15. The config stays repo-scoped; bot loads root config from a base snapshot (packages/nax/src/bot/base-config.ts:98); live status reads root config through its own seam. Match whole first unquoted/unbulleted top-level line case-insensitively; invalid writer rules are reported but do not erase an older valid rule. Honor explicitly wider as well as narrower nonempty lists. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-input.ts:34-103 reads artifact versions 1–3 and selects exact-head artifacts, optionally code-only; no schema/version migration, no historical backfill. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts:337-397 prefers the code review's findings but reconciles settlement and withdrawal against live PR state; a newer conversation-only policy wins when present while the code review still supplies the findings for readiness. Status intentionally uses present comments/config; fix/readiness use saved policy precedence. Older triggers default to normal, unlabeled thread severity to important, older artifacts fall back to config/0, and absence of a ledger leaves lineage unset. US-001 must work before US-002 exists: parse the earlier trigger with the trigger-only primitives locally until US-002 supplies readFindingThreadFacts, then use the shared reader. US-003 owns creation of review-convergence.ts; US-005 extends convergence wiring but does not formally depend on US-003. Preserve the binding graph: keep US-005's history helpers implementable in lineage.ts without US-003's outputs, and compose them into the shared helper when the changes meet; reconcile review-run.ts and post.ts edits rather than adding a dependency or competing policy helper. US-006 can use the explicit blocking-set input and artifact precedence without requiring US-003's new module to be preinstalled; integrate that seam when US-003 is present.

Ledger and Git (US-004/005/006): packages/nax/src/bot/fix-steps.ts:294-320 sets pushedSha after success and preserves outcome nothing for advisor-ledger-only pushes. The ledger append condition is outcome pushed, not merely presence of pushedSha. packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts:581-596 edits one owned fix-summary in place and surfaces write errors; no retry, lock, external ledger, or backfill. packages/nax/src/forge/marker-grammar.ts:12-27 matches only the identity marker; the ledger has a separate grammar and must not change identity. packages/nax/src/bot/ci-waiver-ready.ts:116-155 already preserves non-readiness lines and rewrites the identity wrapper; pin ledger survival in a ready-only test. Extract outcomeText before adding report code (596 lines today, 600 maximum); keep its formatting dependencies out of a fix-report import cycle. Keep new review logic out of the 496-line review runner except wiring. Use last 64 entries and 24,000 encoded characters, safely handle a single oversized entry and corrupt input, and treat retained count as the count of the available ledger, not an all-time counter. packages/nax/src/bot/review-deps.ts:31-47 exposes injectable runGit/isAncestor and distinguishes false from errors. Blame the reviewed head, not uncommitted checkout contents; use reachable entries in ledger order and distinguish per-entry reachability errors (skip/count/warn) from per-target match errors (unknown). For prompt selection distinguish incremental from conversation-only/full, without changing reviewRange (packages/nax/src/bot/review-rulings.ts:203). packages/nax/src/bot/intent.ts:6-22 discovers one unambiguous changed PRD in the checkout; packages/nax/src/prd/index.ts:102 loads it and packages/nax/src/prd/types.ts:204-237 exposes declaration fields.
